title: RISE Live: the venue slice
acceptance: The Reader site's /live page is the venue: a question typed (one field, Enter) or spoken (press-to-talk), RISE's own voice as the clock, the stage's whole instrument with full screen by the browser's API, Settings and sound, and the deterministic mock as the demo without a key.
One real text provider on the reader's own credential: the OpenRouter text-stream adapter on the site's in-memory token flow, listed by the provider registry with no page change.
The Gemini and OpenAI adapters behind a typed, in-memory provider key for a reader who has one, and each verified once against the real service.
No key ever stored or sent anywhere but the chosen provider; the page says whose key it is and what is sent.
One answer, many turns: the reader asks again after a reading ends or while it is held, the room persists, and each reading's journal is carried for perception (design §8 stage 4).

evidence.note: §5 the venue and §8 stage 2, the acceptance above; accepted by the owner 2026-10-09.
§9 Hosts: The venue paragraph (what /live is now, the registry, the test page at ?host=prompt).

Branch live-venue, local run, with venue-entry.test.js, adapters/registry.test.js and stage-controls.test.js: the entry state machine (idle, asking, reading, ended, asking again; typed and spoken; provider choice), the typed key never written to storage, one adapter per room, the room's theme carried; fast unit subset 94 files passed.

Branch live-venue, local production build, headless Chromium, mock provider, paced voice: 'the venue' asks, reads under the whole instrument, asks full screen on F, asks again in the same room with the theme kept, and leaves; with live.spec, live-control, live-voice, live-gemini, live-openai (44 passed), live-mcp field|self-contained (13 passed), visual-catalog, live-red-team, live-eval (14 passed).
The venue page: open, auto-merge on the required CI check. Not merged, not deployed, not accepted.

Branch live-openrouter-adapter, 2026-10-09/10: the shared adapter conformance suite (src/test/live-conformance.js) passes against the OpenRouter adapter with a fake fetch replaying the documented SSE wire; openrouter.test.js (31 tests: refusals 401/402/429 and others, byte-wise chunk splitting, abort, usage, the key absent from every note, journal, event and console line); registry.test.js makes it from the venue registry. Not verified against the real service.
The OpenRouter text-stream adapter, on the reader's own key (branch live-openrouter-adapter), registered in the venue registry.

activity.summary: Venue page built on branch live-venue (Claude, Fable): /live in the app is the venue on the mock and the provider registry; the runtime's test page moves to ?host=prompt. OpenRouter is listed as soon until its adapter lands in the registry. OpenAI is not offered in the venue: its session opens through this site's Worker route, so its key would leave the browser for RISE. No real provider has answered the page.
Venue page opened as #613 (branch live-venue); the OpenRouter adapter half is not yet in.

OpenRouter adapter half (#612, branch live-openrouter-adapter): src/live/adapters/openrouter.js streams OpenRouter chat completions on the in-memory key (ai-connection.js getOpenRouterChat, the adapter never holds it), default model anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5, speaks: 'host'; the venue registry now makes it, so OpenRouter is no longer listed as soon. No real provider has answered.

Both halves are merged and deployed: #612 and #613 are in main at 8007d370, and the live release (rise.syberlabs.io/release.txt read d849025d on 2026-10-10) contains it. Not accepted: the Gemini and OpenAI adapters are still unverified against the real services, and no human has witnessed the venue.

summary: Design §8 stage 2: the first time RISE Live can be felt. The venue page (this branch) and the OpenRouter text-stream adapter (a parallel branch) are its two halves.
